explanation: Aluminium burns in oxygen to form a protective layer of aluminium oxide on its surface.

beaker_view.final_appearance: A dull, greyish-white coating of aluminium oxide on the metal's surface.
beaker_view.observation: Ordinary aluminium doesn't burst into flame the way magnesium does — it just loses its shine as a thin, dull oxide layer forms and seals the surface. (Only finely powdered aluminium, heated strongly, burns with the brilliant white flame this reaction is sometimes associated with.)
